questions.q: How do PCI DSS and HIPAA differ from SOC 2 and ISO 27001 in why they apply to an organization?
options: They are triggered by what data an organization actually handles, not voluntarily chosen to demonstrate trustworthiness
PCI DSS and HIPAA are voluntary attestations chosen to impress customers, just like SOC 2
They only apply to publicly traded companies
They are identical in scope to ISO 27001 and simply use different names
questions.explain: PCI DSS applies because an organization stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data; HIPAA applies because of a covered-entity or business-associate relationship to PHI. Neither is an opt-in attestation like SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

questions.q: What is the Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) under PCI DSS?
options: Only the physical data center where servers are located
A marketing term with no formal compliance meaning
The people, processes, and technology that store, process, or transmit cardholder data, plus anything that could impact its security
The list of customers who have ever used a credit card on the site
questions.explain: The CDE defines PCI DSS scope: the people, process, and technology touching cardholder data, plus connected systems that could affect its security. Scope reduction — isolating the CDE and routing the rest through a validated payment processor — is central to real-world PCI work.

questions.q: Under HIPAA, what makes a vendor a business associate?
options: Simply having a healthcare company as a customer, regardless of what data is involved
Being physically located in the same state as a hospital
Creating, receiving, maintaining, or transmitting Protected Health Information (PHI) on behalf of a covered entity
Having more than 500 employees
questions.explain: A business associate is defined by actually handling PHI on behalf of a covered entity — not by industry label or customer base alone. A vendor that never touches PHI, even if it serves healthcare clients, may not be a business associate at all.

questions.q: What is the practical and legal function of a Business Associate Agreement (BAA)?
options: It is an optional marketing document with no compliance weight
It replaces the need for any technical security controls
It only applies to covered entities, never to the vendors serving them
It is the required contract specifying how a business associate protects PHI, uses it only for permitted purposes, and reports breaches
questions.explain: The BAA is the legal hinge that formalizes a business associate's HIPAA obligations. A vendor that handles PHI without a BAA in place has a serious, independently sanctionable compliance gap.

questions.q: A SaaS company fully outsources checkout to a PCI-validated third-party payment processor and never stores raw cardholder numbers on its own systems. What does this most likely mean?
options: The company automatically becomes HIPAA-covered as a result
The company's own PCI DSS obligation may be significantly reduced or eliminated because its own systems never touch cardholder data
The company must still undergo a full PCI assessment of its entire environment regardless of scope
PCI DSS no longer applies to any company that uses a third-party processor, in every case
questions.explain: Scope reduction by routing card data through a validated processor, so the organization's own systems never see raw PANs, is a real and common way to shrink or eliminate an organization's own CDE-driven PCI obligations — though the exact reduction depends on the specific integration.
